title: CryptoBTB: A Secure Hierarchical BTB for Diverse Instruction Footprint Workloads
problem: Branch Target Buffer (BTB) timing attacks allow adversaries to infer victim BTB updates and mistrain branch predictors, bypassing privilege-level isolation and secure enclave protection; existing encrypted BTB schemes either have security weaknesses or encrypt the BTB index in-pipeline, exposing high latency.
motivation: BTB vulnerabilities have been repeatedly exploited to break process isolation and bypass hardware security boundaries (e.g., Spectre-BTB), and the frequency and diversity of modern workloads—including those with large instruction footprints—make robust, low-overhead BTB security increasingly critical.
method: CryptoBTB proposes a hierarchical exclusive BTB structure where the index encryption is decoupled from the BTB set index computation. The encryption step uses a low-latency scheme that obscures the set mapping without being on the critical prediction path; the hierarchical organization (L1 BTB + L2 BTB) avoids the collision-prone flat structure of prior work (HyBP), allowing the BTB capacity to be better utilized for workloads with large instruction footprints and reducing same-thread collisions.
key_novelty: Decoupling the index encryption from the BTB indexing path enables low-latency secure BTB access while the hierarchical exclusive design recovers the BTB utilization lost by prior schemes that only partially utilize capacity.
contributions: CryptoBTB: secure hierarchical BTB architecture with decoupled low-latency index encryption that prevents set-mapping inference
4.27% average performance overhead vs. 31.89% for HyBP across diverse workload classes
22.57% lower hardware overhead than HyBP while maintaining equivalent security guarantees
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; evaluation covers multiple workload classes but threat model scope and cryptographic strength guarantees relative to adaptive adversaries are not fully detailed in available text.
primary_theme: secure hierarchical BTB with decoupled low-latency index encryption
